text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm seeing an ECC correctable spike in ap-southeast1 GPU pool (gpu-pool-3) starting ~01:10 UTC. Xid entries climbing, ~12% of cards >50 correctables/hr. P99 latency +30ms, customer errors still low but trending. tagging eng-oncall for triage.

ops-bot: [ALERT] ECC_CORRECTABLE_SPIKE detected
pool=ap-southeast1-gpu-pool-3 rate=52/hr threshold=30/hr affected_cards=42 auto_drain=OFF

maria: dropping quick sample from telemetry: ```[gpu0] ecc_correctable=78 xids=12 last_seen=2026-03-17T01:12Z
[gpu1] ecc_correctable=5 xids=0
[gpu2] ecc_correctable=62 xids=7```

alan: thanks. any cluster-level changes recently? kernel/driver/firmware rollouts?

kai: rolled kernel 5.18.14 -> 5.18.15 in that region last night across a subset of hosts (canary then region). saw a few micro-reboots on 3 hosts during rollout window. could be correlated.

shweta: if it's kernel noise, we should avoid bulk hard-drain/replacement — cost + wasteful RMA. prefer soft-drain + cohort replacement. also check card serial ranges.

alan: agree on avoiding wholesale replacement. options: 1) enable soft-autodrain for that pool with a longer cooldown 2) route at-risk traffic to reserved capacity / other regions for latency-sensitive requests 3) cohort-level targeted replacments if serials show sustained >100/hr over 24h.

maria: what's the cost of cross-region failover for a pool of this size? rough ballpark pls.

alan: rough calc: extra egress + instance delta ~ $300/day at current QPS if we shift 30% to other regions. SLA savings probably worth it for critical customers, but not for background batch jobs.

kai: quick query you can run locally to enumerate affected nodes: ```sh
curl -s "https://telemetry.internal/api/v1/pools/ap-southeast1/gpu-pool-3/cards?since=1h" | jq '.[] | {node:.node,serial:.serial,ecc:.ecc_count}'
```

shweta: propose this remediation playbook: 
- 0) set alert suppression window to 5m to reduce flapping
- 1) dry-run annotate affected nodes (label serial prefix) -> `kubectl annotate node <node> ecc-dryrun=true --overwrite`
- 2) enable soft-autodrain on pool with threshold=80/hr, cooldown=10m, max-evict-rate=1/card/hr
- 3) start cross-region routing for latency-sensitive routes only (LRU fallback)
- 4) run kernel rollback on 1 canary host in the pool (5.18.15 -> 5.18.14) and monitor Xid rates for 30m
- 5) open replacement ticket for serials that stay >100/hr over 24h

alan: also add a step: collect nvml logs and Xid dump: `journalctl -u nv_peer_mem -u gpu-driver | grep Xid` and attach to ticket.

maria: I'm going to run the dry-run annotate now and then enable soft-autodrain in dry-run mode. will post results in 10m. @ops-bot can you run a quick capacity check (reserved vs autoscale) for that region?

ops-bot: running capacity check...
- reserved_capacity=176 GPUs
- current_active=164 GPUs
- autoscale_headroom=12 GPUs
- queued_startups=0

kai: with headroom 12, cross-region shift of 30% will saturate remaining capacity. consider spinning temporary burst nodes or failing over only critical routes.

shweta: also recommend limiting auto-drain to nodes with serial prefix `GPX-AP3-` and adding a 24h metric-watch rule before RMA. helps avoid replacing healthy cards hit by transient noise.

alan: +1. And bump alert throttle to avoid repeated ops noise.

maria: result of dry-run annotate: annotated 11 nodes (serials starting GPX-AP3-4*), no evictions executed (dry-run). I'll flip soft-autodrain to dry-run -> enabled and monitor for 15m.

ops-bot: SOFT_AUTODRAIN state=DRY_RUN pool=ap-southeast1-gpu-pool-3 cooldown=10m threshold=80/hr max_evictions_per_hour=1

maria: rolling monitor — P99 and Xid rate in dashboards. ping if you see customer impact.

kai: will rollback kernel on canary host now and report Xid delta in 30m.

shweta: I'll open the replacement ticket template and link telemetry + annotated nodes once we have 24h persistence.

maria: plan acknowledged. final ask: if Xid rate doesn't drop after kernel rollback + 30m, enable selective cross-region failover for API routes with latency SLO < 100ms. otherwise keep soft-drain dry-run.

alan: sounds good. I'll update the pool runbook with the temporary thresholds we discussed.

maria: thanks team. updating incident doc and will leave thread when we have 1h of stable metrics. :thumbsup:
